summary: Fast failover guidance and snapshot-assisted rollback for mixed quantization + tenant-batching profile
description: Issue summary: After applying a tenant-scoped optimizer profile (quantization v2 + aggressive per-request batching overrides) for FinSight Analytics, they observed a 2–5x increase in tail latency for streaming generation requests. Impact: production customers experienced timeouts and degraded UX on chat endpoints during a morning trading window. Environment: dedicated pool (tenanted) in us-west with GPU type A100-80GB, serving model redwood/llama3-8b-quant-v2. Observed: increased p95/p99 token latency to >2s per token, intermittent 502/504s for streamed responses. Expected: modest latency reduction from quantization plus batching. This ticket requests step-by-step safe rollback guidance that minimizes request loss and preserves KV cache state where possible.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) On tenant FinSight, apply optimizer profile 'finsight-quant-batch-v2' via Console -> Tenant Config -> Optimizer Profiles
2) Issue streaming generation requests typical to FinSight workload (avg prompt length ~320 tokens, frequent chat turns).
3) Observe latency spikes in the serving pool; reproduce by replaying a 10m traffic sample through the dedicated endpoint.
4) Confirm 502/504 and stream disconnects in logs and dashboard around the same timestamps.

investigation_notes: Support triaged with FinSight -> confirmed change was an optimizer profile applied only to that tenant at 2026-03-10T08:00:00Z
Replayed the customer's 5m traffic: observed latency increase correlated with batch_size override >32 and quant profile 'v2' that changes kernel selection to 'quant-fused' path
SRE measured higher memory churn and increased KV cache eviction rate when both batching and quantization were enabled together for this model/sequence-length distribution

Hypothesis: the aggressive batching caused larger combined token windows resulting in kernel path that has a micro-serialization step leading to head-of-line latency increases under this tenant's traffic pattern
Alternative hypothesis: quant-fused kernel in v2 interacts poorly with our current caching layout for sequence lengths ~300+, causing repeated cache misses and recompute
Checked dashboards: autoscaler attempted to add workers but hit per-tenant worker limit; observed GPU memory saturation on 2 workers prior to 504s
proposed_safe_rollback_steps: A) Snapshot current runtime state for the tenant: call /admin/tenants/finsight/snapshot (creates kv-cache dump + optimizer metadata). Keep snapshot ID in ticket.
B) Create a canary policy: route 10% of FinSight traffic to a rollback config and 90% to current profile using traffic routing rules in Console. Monitor p95/p99 and 5xxs for 15 minutes.

C) If canary shows improvement, perform a staged rollback: first disable tenant-level batching overrides (set batch_size back to tenant default) while keeping quant profile pinned to previous stable v1.3. Wait 10 minutes and monitor.

D) If step C mitigates, fully revert optimizer profile to 'finsight-quant-stable-v1.3' and keep the snapshot for 48 hours for audit. If not, run fallback: temporarily set model variant to 'redwood/llama3-8b-cpu-fallback' with lower throughput but stable latency for problematic endpoints.

E) After rollback, run a controlled replay of earlier traffic and confirm KV cache warming. If cache miss rate is high, use snapshot to warm caches on new workers (api: /admin/tenants/finsight/warm-cache?snapshot=<ID>).
F) Document follow-up: open INT ticket for optimizer-engine to add compatibility gating for quant-fused kernels when tenant batch overrides exceed 32 for this model family.
G) Communicate plan and ETA to customer (keep them in loop on Slack channel #support-finsight and via email).
actions_taken: 2026-03-10T09:03Z: created snapshot snapshot-20260310-09-03 (admin). 2026-03-10T09:15Z: applied canary routing (10% traffic) and measured p95 drop from 2.1s to 0.9s on canary. 2026-03-10T09:40Z: disabled per-tenant batching override; quant profile pinned to stable v1.3. Observed 5xxs return to baseline and p99 reduced to 1.1s. Kept dedicated pool limits unchanged. Customer ops confirmed improved UX.
resolution: Workaround applied: staged rollback described above completed and customer traffic restored to stable optimizer profile. Root-cause: interaction between quant-fused kernel path and aggressive tenant batch overrides for sequences ~300+. Long-term fix: INT-4522 created to add pre-deploy compatibility checks and a runtime guard that prevents switching to quant-fused kernels when tenant batch_size > 32 for this model family. Ticket will be closed after INT follow-up or when permanent mitigations are rolled out.
postmortem_followup_items: 1) INT-4522: Implement optimizer compatibility checks and preflight validations
2) Update Confluence runbook to include snapshot/warm-cache steps for tenant-scoped rollbacks
3) Add automated alert when per-tenant KV cache eviction rate > 10% over 5m for production pools
4) Schedule cross-team review (serving-runtime + optimizer) to verify kernel interactions with batching thresholds
